definition: Robotics engineering is a branch of engineering that focuses on the conception, design, manufacturing, and operation of robots.
details: It involves a multidisciplinary approach, drawing primarily from mechanical, electrical, software, and artificial intelligence (AI) engineering . Robotics engineers are tasked with designing these robots to function reliably and safely in real-world scenarios, which often require addressing complex mechanical movements, real-time control, and adaptive decision-making through software and AI.

explainer.lead: Robotics engineering covers the conception, design, manufacturing and operation of robots. It matters because robots must work reliably and safely in messy real-world settings.

tiers.eli5: It is the job of building robots from the ground up, mixing mechanics, electronics, software and smart decision-making.
tiers.practitioner: It is multidisciplinary, drawing on mechanical, electrical, software and AI engineering, and engineers must handle complex mechanical movement, real-time control and adaptive decision-making. A pitfall is optimizing one discipline while neglecting the others.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the engineering branch for conception, design, manufacturing and operation of robots, integrating mechanical, electrical, software and AI engineering. Reliability and safety in real-world scenarios are explicit requirements.

explainer.example: A team designing a warehouse robot combines mechanical chassis design, electrical control circuits, real-time software and AI decisions for safe operation.
